label: Dropout stays on at inference time
description:
Dropout is active during training and OFF during inference (unless you're explicitly doing Monte Carlo Dropout for uncertainty estimation). At inference, the network uses all activations; the standard implementation rescales by 1/(1-p) during training (inverted dropout) so the expected output magnitude stays the same.

Getting this wrong silently degrades inference quality. If you forget to set `model.eval()` in PyTorch, dropout (and batch-norm running stats) behave the wrong way and predictions become noisy. The same issue trips people up with weight averaging, EMA models, and any layer with separate train/eval semantics.
probeQuestions: What does PyTorch's `model.eval()` actually toggle? Name two layer types affected.
Why does inverted dropout rescale by 1/(1-p) during training instead of multiplying by (1-p) at inference?
correctionPromptTemplate: The learner thinks dropout stays on at inference. Walk through: dropout is a training-time regularizer that's turned OFF for prediction. Mention the inverted-dropout 1/(1-p) rescaling and why it preserves expected magnitude. Note MC Dropout as the deliberate exception. Ask first — 'why would leaving dropout on at inference hurt accuracy?'
